messages:
alex: Heads-up — during a batch of GPU node provisioning in us-west-2 we're seeing local NVMe remounts and node-drain hangs. 3 hosts hit drain timeouts. Logs pasted below.

alex: ```
Mar 10 03:12:15 host-nvme-12 kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345678
Mar 10 03:12:16 host-nvme-12 kernel: XFS (nvme0n1p1): metadata I/O error
Mar 10 03:12:17 host-nvme-12 systemd: kubelet.service: main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
Mar 10 03:12:18 host-nvme-12 kubelet: evicting pods: unable to cleanly stop containers: mount: remounting /var/lib/kubelet: read-only file system
```

ops-bot: Auto-alert: node i-0abc1234 (host-nvme-12) failed drain (timeout). Incident INC-4321 created.

sam: Noted. Are these spot/ephemeral replacement nodes or long-lived instance-store? Could be accelerated wear from pre-warm or synthetic I/O.

cheng: Checking the kubelet traces — 'Stopping container' stuck because mounts went readonly. Kubelet can't finish pod shutdown. Seems not a kubelet bug, underlying FS remounted ro after I/O errors.

maria: Do we have SMART or nvme-cli output? Would like to see media errors vs controller issues before deciding retire vs reprovision.

alex: Pasted quick smartctl/nvme-cli dump for one host.

alex: ```
# nvme id-ctrl /dev/nvme0 -H
serial-number: NVME202103X12
fw-revision: 1.3.7
critical-warning: 0x02 (available spare below threshold)
media-errors: 34

# smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1
Data Units Written: 12345
Host Write Commands: 987654
Percentage Used: 78%
Errors: 34 reallocated sectors
```

sam: 78% used and 'available spare below threshold' is a red flag. If provisioning pre-warm writes a lot at boot we could push several devices over threshold quickly.

cheng: I also noticed firmware mismatch: two hosts on 1.2.4, one on 1.3.7. Controller bug in 1.2.x is known to cause stale metadata under intense parallel writes on some decks. I'll open a remediation play to standardize FW and run nvme-format/secure-erase as part of retire flow.

drain-bot: Drain job 4567: force-delete pods on i-0abc1234 completed — 12 pods evicted, 2 pods failed -> scheduled retry.

maria: For the immediate cluster health we should avoid full drain attempts on nodes that report 'readonly remount'. Suggest cordon + force-delete pods that are stateless, and mark block-storage-backed pods for migration.

alex: We tried `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=120` and kubelet never finishes because mountpoints flip to ro mid-shutdown. Workaround: cordon + `kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0` for non-critical workloads. Still want an automated safe path.

sam: On cost/process side: we have pre-warm script that writes 8k random to full device with dd for 10 minutes. Can we switch to sparse write + read-verify with lower concurrency? I'll prototype a throttled prewarm.

alex: Action items:
- disable the aggressive pre-warm in us-west-2 provisioning pipeline (temporary)
- add SMART + fw-version check to provisioning gating (fail fast if spare% < 20 or media-errors > 0)
- add emergency runbook for 'readonly remount' that does cordon + selective force-evict and tags node for hardware inspection

cheng: I'll draft the FW remediation play and add a step to the retire workflow to secure-erase device before handing back to pool. That should reduce phantom corruption on re-use.

maria: Ops note — enable IOPS cgroup throttling on startup to limit prewarm concurrency. Should cut peak IOPS by ~50% and likely avoid triggering controller protective remounts.

sam: I'll prototype a prewarm with: `fio --name=prewarm --rw=write --bs=256k --iodepth=8 --size=500M --rate_iops=2000` and test on canary.

alex: Thanks, all. I've updated INC-4321 with timeline + temp mitigations. Please add any logs to the ticket. :thumbsup:
